## Introduction

In this tutorial, we will learn how to use the ESP32 as a simple web server.

Instead of sending data over the serial monitor, the ESP32 will create its own Wi-Fi network and host a small web page that you can open from your phone or laptop. This web page can:

- **display information** (for example, temperature and humidity), and  
- **receive input** (for example, a button click to turn an led on or off).

We will focus on three examples:

1. A web server that shows temperature and humidity from the SHT31 sensor.
1. A web server that controls the built-in led.
1. A web server that logs SHT31 readings in memory and lets you download them as a CSV file.

All examples work without any external Wi-Fi network. The ESP32 itself creates the Wi-Fi network.

## SHT31 data logger on web server

This example reads temperature and humidity once a second and keeps every reading in the ESP32's own memory (an array, not a file). Open the web page to see the latest reading and how many samples have been stored so far, then click the download link to fetch everything collected as a `data.csv` file.

The buffer has a fixed size (`maxSamples`, 3600 by default — one hour at one reading per second). Once it's full, logging stops until the board is reset.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
code_source("SHT31_logger_server.ino")
```
